articleBlocks: At first, Apple and Dell pointed in a few different directions, so the board still felt wider than one exact category.

One tempting read was "a broader umbrella topic". Apple, Dell can point toward several nearby themes before one clue makes the exact category level visible. Lenovo is the clue that narrows the board into one category with clearer boundaries.

Another nearby read was "a one-clue surface theme". Early clues often tempt you to overfit the board around one obvious surface similarity. The final answer works because it keeps every clue at the same level of specificity, not because one clue happens to fit first.
Once I read the set through a category board focused on computer makers, examples like "Apple as a PC maker" and "Dell as a PC maker" stopped feeling loose and started landing cleanly.
Acer, HP, Lenovo keep the clues at the same category level, which is what makes the board feel like one exact set instead of a broad umbrella theme.

The answer was "Manufacturers of personal computers". More precisely, all five clues name companies known for designing and selling PCs, which fits better than a broad technology or electronics theme.
solutionNarrative: I started by testing Apple and Dell, but that only gave me a loose direction. I initially drifted toward a broader umbrella topic, because the first clues could still fit several nearby ideas. I held the guess until one clue gave me a more specific way to read the list.
The turn came when I let "Lenovo" lead the solve. After that, Acer and HP became the real confirmation check, because they had to fit the same idea without changing the rule or stretching the answer.

For the final pass, I checked Apple, Dell, Acer, HP, Lenovo one by one. The answer worked only if the whole list could stay inside one tight reading, not because one early clue happened to match a broad topic.
The answer was "Manufacturers of personal computers".
